audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows contradicted their own whys: Level 1 was Lillia while whys[0] says Poppy has the point-and-click reliability, Level 3 was Poppy while whys[2] says neither side owns it, Levels 4-5 was Poppy while whys[3] calls it the window she kites you down, Level 6 was Lillia while whys[4] says it stays even, and first item was Poppy while whys[5] says she edges it.
audit.why: The prose was correct and the tokens were not, so the page answered 'who wins Level 1' two different ways.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Poppy / Skill / Skill / Lillia / Skill / Lillia / Poppy in matched full/content pairs, ratings rescaled to 7, 6, 5, 4, 5, 4, 6. Identical to the audited lillia__poppy mirror.

audit.why: Four spikes present — levels 1-2, levels 4-5 kite window, level 6 sleep, 2+ items — and they line up with the corrected chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Your W deletes dashes' is the headline in tldr, winCon, report[0], report[1], tradeGood, dosFull[1].d and phases[1].why. Lillia has no dash in her kit — her mobility is the stacking move speed on Blooming Blows, which Steadfast Presence does not touch. The content layer already says this ('she has no dash to ground') and the full layer contradicts it.
audit.why: A player holding a 20s W as a parry against a champion who never dashes loses the ability entirely; the real use here is W's move speed to close.
audit.corrected: Every dash-deny claim replaced: Lillia has no dash, W is your gap-closer, and the lane is landing Heroic Charge on terrain. Added the interaction that was missing — the edge of Blooming Blows deals true damage, so armour does not read the trade.
